sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: A few short years ago, if you needed to buy something,
sentences.zh: 就在几年前，如果你需要买东西，

sentences.en: you would take a walk down to a corner shop or go to a mall.
sentences.zh: 你会步行去街角的商店或去商场。

sentences.en: If you wanted to watch a movie, you went to a theater.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看电影，你会去电影院。

sentences.en: On nights you didn't want to cook, you stepped out to a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 在不想做饭的晚上，你会出门去餐馆。

sentences.en: Shopping, entertainment, and dining brought us into contact with other people.
sentences.zh: 购物、娱乐和用餐让我们与他人产生接触。

sentences.en: Waiting in line at checkout or standing in a crowded bar,
sentences.zh: 在结账排队时，或站在拥挤的酒吧里，

sentences.en: we encountered a wide spectrum of humanity.
sentences.zh: 我们接触到了形形色色的人。

sentences.en: Nice people, mean people, boring people.
sentences.zh: 好人、刻薄的人、无聊的人。

sentences.en: Today, many of us choose convenience and comfort over connection.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们许多人选择便利和舒适，而非人际连接。

sentences.en: Need something from the grocery store?
sentences.zh: 需要从杂货店买东西吗？

sentences.en: Plug your order into your phone.
sentences.zh: 在手机上下单即可。

sentences.en: Want to see a movie?
sentences.zh: 想看电影吗？

sentences.en: Fire up Netflix on your computer.
sentences.zh: 在电脑上打开 Netflix。

sentences.en: Need to check in on friends?
sentences.zh: 需要联系朋友吗？

sentences.en: Hop on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 刷刷 Instagram。

sentences.en: You can pay someone to walk your dog or stand in line for you at a concert.
sentences.zh: 你可以花钱雇人帮你遛狗，或者在音乐会现场替你排队。

sentences.en: Dating apps allow you to check out potential mates
sentences.zh: 约会软件让你可以在沙发上安全地

sentences.en: from the safety of your couch.
sentences.zh: 挑选潜在的伴侣。

sentences.en: Why go out when you can order in?
sentences.zh: 既然可以点外卖，何必出门呢？

sentences.en: Some time ago, the food delivery app Seamless launched an ad campaign
sentences.zh: 前些年，外卖应用 Seamless 发起了一场广告活动，

sentences.en: plastering signs all over the New York City subway.
sentences.zh: 把广告贴满了纽约地铁的各个角落。

sentences.en: In bright colors with big yellow font, the ads read,
sentences.zh: 广告用鲜艳的颜色和醒目的黄色字体写道：

sentences.en: over 8 million people in New York City, and we help you avoid them all.
sentences.zh: “纽约市有超过 800 万人，而我们帮你避开他们所有人。”

sentences.en: How did we get here?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: When did the world become a place where friendship meant liking a photo?
sentences.zh: 世界是从什么时候开始变成了一个“点赞照片即代表友谊”的地方？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the source of the powerful vortex that warps the way we feel
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨那股扭曲我们对世界感受的强大漩涡的来源，

sentences.en: about the world, and how to fight its gravitational pull.
sentences.zh: 以及如何对抗它的引力。

sentences.en: We are all born with eyes filled with wonder.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人出生时，眼中都充满了惊奇。

sentences.en: We play, we laugh, we seek out friends.
sentences.zh: 我们玩耍，我们欢笑，我们寻找朋友。

sentences.en: But at some point, this changes.
sentences.zh: 但到了某个时刻，这一切改变了。

sentences.en: We erect defenses against the world.
sentences.zh: 我们开始对世界竖起防线。

sentences.en: We pull back from strangers.
sentences.zh: 我们开始疏远陌生人。

sentences.en: We retreat into ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们退缩进自己的内心世界。

sentences.en: What was that moment for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，那个时刻是什么时候？

sentences.en: Was it when you got bullied in middle school?
sentences.zh: 是你在中学被霸凌的时候吗？

sentences.en: When a friend betrayed your trust?
sentences.zh: 是朋友背叛你信任的时候吗？

sentences.en: When the grind of living paycheck to paycheck became too much?
sentences.zh: 是入不敷出的生活压力变得难以承受的时候吗？

sentences.en: At Stanford University, psychologist Jamil Zaki is interested in how our experiences shape
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，心理学家贾米尔·扎基对我们的经历如何塑造

sentences.en: our view of the world, and how our view of the world shapes what we experience.
sentences.zh: 我们的世界观，以及我们的世界观如何塑造我们的经历很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Jamil Zaki, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 贾米尔·扎基，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Jamil, some time ago, you came across a story about a young Japanese artiSt.
sentences.zh: 贾米尔，前些时候，你偶然发现了一位年轻日本艺术家的故事。

sentences.en: He said he had discovered something about himself on a New Year's Eve.
sentences.zh: 他说他在一个除夕夜发现了关于自己的一些事情。

sentences.en: Who was this young man, and what was his story?
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人是谁？他的故事是什么？

sentences.en: His name is Atsushi Watanabe.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫渡边笃。

sentences.en: He's an artist living in Japan, and he, through a long series of events, had become quite isolated,
sentences.zh: 他是一位居住在日本的艺术家，在一系列漫长的事件后，他变得非常孤立，

sentences.en: and in fact was isolated entirely in his room for many months.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在房间里完全与世隔绝了许多个月。

sentences.en: He had begun his period of isolation during a day in July, which in Japan is known as
sentences.zh: 他开始这段隔离期是在七月的一天，在日本被称为

sentences.en: Sea Day, or Umi no He.
sentences.zh: “海之日”。

sentences.en: And on New Year's Eve, he was on a streaming site, and he saw somebody else on that site
sentences.zh: 在除夕夜，他正在一个流媒体网站上，看到网站上另一个人

sentences.en: comment, the last time I saw the sky was Sea Day, meaning that this person had been isolated
sentences.zh: 评论说：“我上次看到天空还是在海之日”，这意味着这个人已经与世隔绝

sentences.en: and inside for nearly six months.
sentences.zh: 并待在室内近六个月了。

sentences.en: And Watanabe realized, with horror, that that was true of him as well.
sentences.zh: 渡边惊恐地意识到，他自己也是如此。

sentences.en: Atsushi Watanabe grew up about 25 miles outside of Tokyo, in a city called Yokohama.
sentences.zh: 渡边笃在距离东京约 25 英里的横滨市长大。

sentences.en: His life was chaotic.
sentences.zh: 他的生活很混乱。

sentences.en: He fought with his sister, and according to Atsushi, his father did not get along with the
sentences.zh: 他和姐姐吵架，据渡边说，他的父亲与周围的人

sentences.en: people around him, and his mother didn't do much to alleviate the situation.
sentences.zh: 相处不好，而他的母亲也没有采取什么措施来缓解这种情况。

sentences.en: So he felt very embittered and disappointed towards them.
sentences.zh: 所以他感到非常痛苦，对他们感到失望。

sentences.en: He was very talented from a young age at art and crafts, and sort of escaped into art, and
sentences.zh: 他从小在艺术和手工艺方面就非常有天赋，某种程度上逃避到了艺术中，

sentences.en: found that that became a career for him.
sentences.zh: 并发现这成为了他的职业。

sentences.en: He went to a specialized high school, and then to Tokyo University of the Arts, and really
sentences.zh: 他进入了一所专业高中，然后进入了东京艺术大学，在童年和成年早期

sentences.en: created beautiful works throughout his childhood and early adulthood.
sentences.zh: 确实创作出了美丽的作品。

sentences.en: I mean, that sounds wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, he was pursuing a career as an artiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他当时正在追求艺术家的职业生涯。

sentences.en: It sounds wonderful.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: For him, it was more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，情况比这复杂得多。

sentences.en: Watanabe really wanted his art to help people.
sentences.zh: 渡边真心希望他的艺术能帮助他人。

sentences.en: He wanted to use it as social commentary.
sentences.zh: 他想将其作为一种社会评论。

sentences.en: And he thought that others in the art world would likewise be driven by these values of
sentences.zh: 他认为艺术界的其他人也会同样被这些关于

sentences.en: connection and altruism.
sentences.zh: 连接和利他的价值观所驱动。

sentences.en: Instead, he found that art, like any other career, is full of careerists, people who are
sentences.zh: 相反，他发现艺术和任何其他职业一样，充满了功利主义者，这些人

sentences.en: often quite competitive and compare themselves to each other.
sentences.zh: 往往竞争心很强，并且喜欢互相攀比。

sentences.en: Watanabe, like so many of us, suffered from depression and anxiety, and being put in this
sentences.zh: 渡边和我们许多人一样，患有抑郁症和焦虑症，而身处这个

sentences.en: pressure cooker of an industry just made it worse and worse, and eventually it became
sentences.zh: 高压锅般的行业只会让情况变得越来越糟，最终变得

sentences.en: unbearable for him.
sentences.zh: 让他无法忍受。

sentences.en: At one point, after seeing so many of his peers posting about their awards, he ended up breaking
sentences.zh: 有一次，在看到许多同龄人发布他们获奖的消息后，他最终摔碎了

sentences.en: his phone and retreating to his parents' home, a place that he wanted to use as an escape,
sentences.zh: 手机，退回到了父母家，他本想把那里当作避难所，

sentences.en: but which really wasn't that comforting for him because his relationship with his parents
sentences.zh: 但那里对他来说其实并不怎么令人宽慰，因为他与父母的关系

sentences.en: was still so strained.
sentences.zh: 依然非常紧张。

sentences.en: So at what point did he withdraw to his room and become essentially a recluse?
sentences.zh: 那么，他是在什么时候退缩到房间里，本质上成为一个隐士的呢？

sentences.en: I believe it was in 2010, and he again started feeling more and more alienated, first from
sentences.zh: 我相信是在 2010 年，他再次开始感到越来越疏远，首先是疏远

sentences.en: the art world, and then more and more from even his family.
sentences.zh: 艺术界，然后甚至越来越疏远他的家人。

sentences.en: I think of his life, and this is from an outsider's perspective, as shrinking, like the
sentences.zh: 我想到他的生活，这是从局外人的角度来看，就像在萎缩，就像

sentences.en: circumference of a circle, becoming smaller and smaller, until the only place that he felt
sentences.zh: 圆的周长，变得越来越小，直到他唯一感到

sentences.en: safe and comfortable was in this tiny, few square feet of his room.
sentences.zh: 安全和舒适的地方就是他房间里那几平方英尺的狭小空间。

sentences.en: He had joined what could be thought of as a community, really having an experience known
sentences.zh: 他加入了一个可以被认为是社区的群体，实际上经历了一种被称为

sentences.en: as hikikomori, a Japanese term for total social isolation.
sentences.zh: “蛰居族”（hikikomori）的状态，这是日本对完全社会隔离的术语。

sentences.en: It's almost like being in a jail cell, except it's a cell of your own creation, as opposed
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是在监狱牢房里，只不过这是一个你自己创造的牢房，而不是

sentences.en: to something imposed on you by the state.
sentences.zh: 国家强加给你的。

sentences.en: How does the story unfold, Jamil?
sentences.zh: 故事是如何发展的，贾米尔？

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he stayed in isolation for months after that, and again, from an outsider's perspective,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那之后他又隔离了几个月，同样，从局外人的角度来看，

sentences.en: it seems like this circumference of your mind shrinks as well.
sentences.zh: 似乎你的思想周长也在萎缩。

sentences.en: Watanabe began to fear that maybe he and the world would never reconnect again, that maybe
sentences.zh: 渡边开始担心，也许他和世界再也无法重新连接了，也许

sentences.en: he would live the rest of his life in that one room.
sentences.zh: 他余生都会在那一个房间里度过。

sentences.en: At some point, his family decided to launch something of an intervention.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，他的家人决定发起某种干预。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, his father, who he had never gotten along with, decided he had had enough, and he contracted
sentences.zh: 是的，他一直合不来的父亲决定受够了，他联系了

sentences.en: with a service in Japan that specializes in involuntarily pulling recluses out of their
sentences.zh: 日本一家专门负责将隐士强行从家中拉出来的服务机构，

sentences.en: homes, and Watanabe, upon learning about this from his mother, was infuriated.
sentences.zh: 而渡边从母亲那里得知此事后，勃然大怒。

sentences.en: He broke down his door and set out to confront his family, but there was no one there.
sentences.zh: 他撞开门，准备去和家人对质，但那里没有人。

sentences.en: They were out for the day.
sentences.zh: 他们白天出去了。

sentences.en: What he did find surprised him.
sentences.zh: 他发现的东西让他感到惊讶。

sentences.en: He found in the living room a lot of books that he had never seen, and paging through
sentences.zh: 他在客厅里发现了很多他从未见过的书，翻阅

sentences.en: them, he realized that his mother had bought all these books about social isolation in
sentences.zh: 这些书时，他意识到母亲买了很多关于社会隔离的书，

sentences.en: an attempt to understand and support her son.
sentences.zh: 试图去理解并支持她的儿子。

sentences.en: And that moment of realizing that in her own way she was trying her best to be there for
sentences.zh: 那一刻，意识到她正以自己的方式尽最大努力陪伴

sentences.en: him, really broke down his defenses.
sentences.zh: 他，真的打破了他的防线。

sentences.en: She came home, and they sat and talked for hours, opening up about the pain that they had
sentences.zh: 她回家了，他们坐下来谈了几个小时，敞开心扉谈论他们所经历的

sentences.en: been through and how they might move forward.
sentences.zh: 痛苦，以及他们如何才能继续前行。

sentences.en: He had not spoken in so long that his throat dried up in trying to speak, and he had to drink
sentences.zh: 他已经很久没有说话了，以至于在试图说话时喉咙干涩，他不得不喝

sentences.en: lots of water even to be able to have this conversation.
sentences.zh: 大量的水才能进行这次谈话。

sentences.en: But he said that at that moment, the captivity of his heart went away for good.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，那一刻，他内心的囚禁彻底消失了。

sentences.en: What happened to Atsushi over the ensuing months?
sentences.zh: 在随后的几个月里，渡边笃发生了什么？

sentences.en: How has he turned out since then, Jamil?
sentences.zh: 贾米尔，从那以后他变得怎么样了？

sentences.en: Atsushi is, to me, an absolute inspiration and a redemption story.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，渡边是一个绝对的灵感来源，也是一个救赎的故事。

sentences.en: He went to a clinic to rehabilitate his body and mind for several months, and then he turned
sentences.zh: 他去了一家诊所进行了几个月的身心康复，然后他将

sentences.en: his period of isolation into art.
sentences.zh: 自己的隔离期转化为了艺术。

sentences.en: In one of his first pieces, he built a concrete structure and isolated himself in it for seven
sentences.zh: 在他最早的作品之一中，他建造了一个混凝土结构，并将自己隔离在其中七天，

sentences.en: days, and then at the end of the seven days, with a hammer, broke himself out of his captivity.
sentences.zh: 七天结束后，他用一把锤子把自己从囚禁中解救出来。

sentences.en: And what I find so beautiful about this is that he was mimicking the experience of isolation,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这最美妙的地方在于，他是在模仿隔离的经历，

sentences.en: but owning it, transmuting it into something that other people could understand.
sentences.zh: 但却掌控了它，将其转化为其他人可以理解的东西。

sentences.en: And this time, instead of opening the door into his living room, when he escaped his
sentences.zh: 这一次，当他逃离囚禁时，不再是打开通往客厅的门，

sentences.en: captivity, there were photographers and an audience, and his art has inspired so many.
sentences.zh: 而是有摄影师和观众在场，他的艺术激励了许多人。

sentences.en: He's made lots of pieces like this, bringing awareness to the pain of isolation, and has
sentences.zh: 他创作了许多这样的作品，让人们意识到隔离的痛苦，并

sentences.en: become an extremely successful and in-demand artist in Japan.
sentences.zh: 在日本成为了一位极其成功且炙手可热的艺术家。

sentences.en: So about 300 miles from where Atsushi lived in Tokyo is the city of Kobe.
sentences.zh: 距离渡边居住的东京约 300 英里处是神户市。

sentences.en: You talk about two Japanese neighborhoods in Kobe.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了神户的两个日本社区。

sentences.en: They were only a few miles apart, but they were also very different.
sentences.zh: 它们相距仅几英里，但却截然不同。

sentences.en: How's so, Jamil?
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样，贾米尔？

sentences.en: Yeah, so these are two neighborhoods known as Mano and Mikura.
sentences.zh: 是的，这两个社区被称为真野（Mano）和御藏（Mikura）。

sentences.en: On paper, pretty similar, both working-class neighborhoods with lots of factories, for instance.
sentences.zh: 从纸面上看，它们非常相似，都是拥有许多工厂的工人阶级社区。

sentences.en: But they had different histories.
sentences.zh: 但它们有着不同的历史。

sentences.en: Mano had a lot of family businesses and a lot of local trade between people who were also neighbors.
sentences.zh: 真野有很多家族企业，邻里之间有很多本地贸易。

sentences.en: It also had a history of activism.
sentences.zh: 它还有着行动主义的历史。

sentences.en: People in Mano had fought for environmental protection, for instance, together.
sentences.zh: 例如，真野的人们曾共同为环境保护而战。

sentences.en: And that had bonded them in common cause over the decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，这使他们为了共同的事业而团结在一起。

sentences.en: So you can think of Mano as a very tight-knit, trusting, and interdependent community.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以把真野看作是一个非常紧密、相互信任和相互依赖的社区。

sentences.en: Mikura had less of that history, and people were less connected, less interdependent, and
sentences.zh: 御藏则缺乏那样的历史，人们之间的联系较少，相互依赖性较弱，

sentences.en: potentially less trusting of one another as well.
sentences.zh: 彼此之间的信任度也可能较低。

sentences.en: So in 1995, a massive earthquake hit Kobe and its surrounding neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 1995 年，一场大地震袭击了神户及其周边社区。

sentences.en: The tremors sparked fires that lasted for days and destroyed over 100,000 buildings.
sentences.zh: 震动引发了持续数天的大火，摧毁了超过 10 万座建筑物。

sentences.en: More than 6,000 people died.
sentences.zh: 超过 6000 人死亡。

sentences.en: What happened to these two neighborhoods, Jamil?
sentences.zh: 贾米尔，这两个社区发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a horrible tragedy, but really, if you think about it and look at the historical
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一场可怕的悲剧，但如果你仔细思考并查看历史

sentences.en: record, it was more than one tragedy, because it was experienced so differently by these different
sentences.zh: 记录，这不仅仅是一场悲剧，因为这些不同的社区对它的经历截然不同。

sentences.en: neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 社区。

sentences.en: In Mikura, people watched often in their nightclothes, in their pajamas, while buildings were reduced
sentences.zh: 在御藏，人们经常穿着睡衣，在睡衣里看着建筑物化为

sentences.en: to ash.
sentences.zh: 灰烬。

sentences.en: In Mano, people did not wait for the authorities.
sentences.zh: 而在真野，人们没有等待当局的救援。

sentences.en: They banded together and fought the fires themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们团结起来，自己扑灭了大火。

sentences.en: For instance, running hoses from factories or creating pop-up bucket brigades to bring

sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，心理学家贾米尔·扎基对我们看待世界的方式如何

sentences.zh: 即认为人们普遍贪婪、不诚实且不可信。

sentences.zh: 几年前的一项调查发现，12年级的学生，也就是刚步入

sentences.zh: 成年的人，比老一辈人更缺乏信任感。

sentences.zh: 他的一些研究，关于父母为了保护孩子，教导他们

sentences.zh: 世界是一个危险的地方。

sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你认为父母和其他监护人是否应该为孩子

sentences.zh: 变得不信任他人承担部分责任？

sentences.zh: 正如你所描述的，他采访了数百名父母，问他们，你认为什么

sentences.zh: 对你的孩子有帮助？

sentences.zh: 你认为什么样的信念对他们有帮助？

sentences.en: And more than half believed that in order to help their child, they should make them feel
sentences.zh: 超过一半的人认为，为了帮助孩子，他们应该让他们觉得

sentences.zh: 世界是危险的，而不是安全的。

sentences.en: And I want to say, I can really understand why a parent would feel that.
sentences.zh: 我想说，我真的很理解父母为什么会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: As a parent, I felt that way too.
sentences.zh: 作为一名家长，我也曾有过这种感觉。

sentences.en: We think it's our job to protect our children from the slings and arrows of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们认为保护孩子免受世界的伤害是我们的职责。

sentences.en: But it turns out that if you teach your children that the world is full of slings and arrows,
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，如果你教导孩子世界充满了伤害，

sentences.zh: 他们就会时刻带着盾牌生活。

sentences.en: And that might not actually help them.
sentences.zh: 而这可能并不能真正帮助他们。

sentences.en: So by teaching our kids that the world is dangerous, we might be keeping them safer from
sentences.zh: 所以，通过教导孩子世界是危险的，我们可能让他们免受了

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.en: So as you just said, a number of studies show that people with lower trust tend to be less
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才所说，许多研究表明，信任度较低的人往往比信任度较高的人

sentences.en: happy, less healthy, less engaged in their communities compared with people who have higher levels
sentences.zh: 更不快乐、更不健康、在社区中参与度更低。

sentences.en: of truSt.
sentences.zh: 信任。

sentences.zh: 经济学家已经在全国范围内衡量了信任的影响，并对

sentences.zh: 各国进行了比较。

sentences.en: What do they find, Jamil?
sentences.zh: 他们发现了什么，贾米尔？

sentences.en: Yeah, trust at a social level is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 是的，社会层面的信任极其重要。

sentences.en: Of course, if you as a person can trust, that's good for you.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你个人能够信任他人，这对你有好处。

sentences.zh: 如果我们作为一个群体能够信任彼此，这对我们所有人都有好处。

sentences.zh: 表现得非常灵活，能够迅速调整。

sentences.en: But trust helps us in good times as well.
sentences.zh: 但信任在顺境中也同样能帮助我们。

sentences.zh: 信任度高的国家，人们往往更愿意参与志愿服务和慈善捐赠，

sentences.zh: 他们的国民幸福感往往更高，经济表现也往往更好。

sentences.en: Economists once measured the trust of dozens of nations and then the growth in their GDP

sentences.zh: 它们的GDP增长情况。

sentences.zh: 低信任度国家的经济则停滞不前甚至萎缩。

sentences.zh: 我发现其中一个统计数据非常惊人，即在幸福感方面，

sentences.zh: 生活在一个高信任度的群体中，其价值相当于加薪40%。

sentences.en: That's incredible, Jamil.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了，贾米尔。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And again, I think it comes back to this beautiful metaphor you raised earlier of social infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这又回到了你之前提到的社会基础设施这个美妙的比喻。

sentences.en: If you feel as though you are part of a community, evidence shows from so many angles that that
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得你是社区的一部分，多方面的证据表明，这

sentences.en: is salutary, positive for both your physical and mental health.
sentences.zh: 对你的身心健康都是有益且积极的。

sentences.en: So cynics turn out to be highly critical of others and themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，犬儒主义者最终会对他人和自己都持高度批判态度。

sentences.en: And you say that even though you were running a lab studying empathy, you fell into this
sentences.zh: 你说过，尽管你当时经营着一个研究同理心的实验室，但你在斯坦福教书的

sentences.en: trap yourself the first year that you were teaching at Stanford.

sentences.zh: 你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a story that I'm not very proud of, but I think is important to tell.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个我不太引以为傲，但我认为有必要讲述的故事。

sentences.en: So I started at Stanford in 2012 and was extremely anxious.
sentences.zh: 我2012年开始在斯坦福工作，当时非常焦虑。

sentences.en: You know, this is the job that I dreamed of my entire adult life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我成年后一直梦想的工作。

sentences.zh: 最终，它落到了我头上。

sentences.zh: 当你创办实验室时，另一件事就是你不再仅仅

sentences.zh: 依赖你自己了。

sentences.zh: 你依赖于你雇佣的人。

sentences.zh: 就我而言，是博士后、研究生和员工。

sentences.en: I figured that my job was to absolutely, in an anxiety-ridden way, make sure that everyone
sentences.zh: 我想我的工作就是以一种焦虑的方式，确保每个人

sentences.zh: 都像我需要的那样高效，并且像他们需要的那样成功，

sentences.zh: 方式和我完全一样。

sentences.en: I think that I was probably a very stressful person to have as a leader.
sentences.zh: 我想作为一个领导者，我可能是一个让人压力很大的人。

sentences.en: And actually, I don't just think that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我不只是这么想。

sentences.en: I know it.
sentences.zh: 我知道是这样。

sentences.en: About a year into the life of my lab, one of the people that I was trying to train urgently
sentences.zh: 在我实验室运行大约一年后，我试图培养的一名成员紧急

sentences.en: requested a meeting.
sentences.zh: 要求开会。

sentences.en: And so we met.
sentences.zh: 于是我们见了面。

sentences.en: And she was in tears and said, you know, this work is really stressing me out.
sentences.zh: 她泪流满面地说，你知道，这项工作真的让我压力很大。

sentences.en: And it's just unsustainable for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说这简直无法承受。

sentences.en: I feel as though my mental health is taking a hit in this lab.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的心理健康在这个实验室里受到了打击。

sentences.en: And if things don't change, I'm going to leave.
sentences.zh: 如果情况不改变，我就要离开了。

sentences.en: Frankly, Shankar, I feel some shame, almost a visceral response, even talking about it
sentences.zh: 坦白说，尚卡尔，我现在谈起这件事，甚至有一种羞耻感，几乎是本能的反应。

sentences.en: now.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 但这确实很引人深思，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you're an empathy researcher and you've created something of a toxic environment in
sentences.zh: 因为你是一名同理心研究员，却在自己的实验室里创造了

sentences.zh: 某种有毒的环境。

sentences.zh: 也就是说，这种不匹配一定非常令人震惊。

sentences.en: It was a rich and very painful irony that I felt immediately.
sentences.zh: 这是一种丰富且非常痛苦的讽刺，我立刻就感受到了。

sentences.en: And I have to say, I'm extremely grateful to that person for having the bravery to step
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我非常感谢那个人，因为她有勇气站出来

sentences.zh: 挑战当时的新老板。

sentences.zh: 我从那一刻学到了很多，并做出了改变。

sentences.zh: 但在当时，我意识到我的犬儒主义不仅让我陷入困境，

sentences.zh: 那确实是一个非常艰难的认识。

sentences.en: I should say, Jamil, that, you know, I've known you now for a few years.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，贾米尔，你知道，我认识你已经几年了。

sentences.en: And I think you are one of the kindest and most generous people that I know.
sentences.zh: 我认为你是我认识的最善良、最慷慨的人之一。

sentences.en: So I have no doubt that in some ways you've learned from these experiences and changed.
sentences.zh: 所以我毫不怀疑，在某些方面你已经从这些经历中吸取了教训并做出了改变。

sentences.en: But it is striking that many of the qualities that you describe that cynics have, a tendency
sentences.zh: 但令人震惊的是，你描述的犬儒主义者的许多特质，比如倾向于

sentences.en: to withdraw into themselves or to be distrustful or to be highly critical, these are things
sentences.zh: 退缩到自己的世界，或者不信任他人，或者高度批判，这些都是你

sentences.zh: 在自己身上发现的东西？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.zh: 而且我认为这背后有很多原因。

sentences.zh: 愤世嫉俗者往往是过去曾受过伤害的人。

sentences.zh: 嗯，我的家庭生活相对比较艰难。

sentences.zh: 为了生存而保护自己的想法。

sentences.zh: 嗯，如今我把自己看作一个正在康复的愤世嫉俗者，因为我，我，我，我，我，我，

sentences.zh: 我正在努力改善自己的这些特质，即使我还在尝试教导别人如何应对这些特质。

sentences.en: uh, domains.
sentences.zh: 嗯，各个领域。

sentences.zh: 嗯，其中最引人注目的是在教育领域。

sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，心理学家沃尔特·库克（Walter Cook）和唐纳德·梅德利（Donald Medley）询问老师们是否

sentences.zh: 同意三个陈述。
